response.title: how much does a whole house battery backup cost
response.answer:
A whole-house battery backup system typically costs $15,000–$40,000 installed in the United States, depending on your home's electricity consumption, how long you want backup power, and whether you already have solar panels.

For a typical 2,000–3,000 sq. ft. house, I'd budget around $20,000–$30,000 for a system that can power most household needs through an overnight outage.

markup:
A **whole-house battery backup system typically costs $15,000–$40,000 installed** in the United States, depending on your home's electricity consumption, how long you want backup power, and whether you already have solar panels.

For a typical 2,000–3,000 sq. ft. house, I'd budget around **$20,000–$30,000** for a system that can power most household needs through an overnight outage.

## Cost by battery system size

| Battery capacity | Estimated installed cost | Typical use |
|---|---:|---|
| 10–15 kWh | $10,000–$18,000 | Essential circuits, limited whole-home use |
| 20–30 kWh | $18,000–$30,000 | Most household loads for roughly 12–24 hours |
| 40–60 kWh | $30,000–$50,000 | Larger homes or longer outages |
| 80–100 kWh | $55,000–$85,000+ | High consumption or multi-day backup |

These are approximate U.S. planning estimates, before any applicable incentives. Actual backup duration depends heavily on air conditioning, electric heating, EV charging, and other large loads.

One important consideration: **you don't need solar panels to install batteries.** They can charge from the grid, but solar panels can recharge them during a prolonged outage. Also, the federal homeowner tax credit for new battery installations ended after 2025, although some state and utility incentives remain. <Cite refs={["turn263689search0","turn263689search4"]}/>
